A '''warehouse store''' was located in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]], [[Capital/Legends|capital]] city of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. Owned by a [[Unidentified Mandalorian warehouse owner|Mandalorian woman]], and housed within a large warehouse facility, the Keldabe retailer stocked and sold a variety of used [[Droid/Legends|droid]] parts and specialty equipment. The store was staffed by the Mandalorian business owner, along with a [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] who manned a desk in the storefront lobby and greeted potential customers. The business's expansive inventory was kept inside the building's large warehouse facility, stocked on shelving racks and in hanging nets that rose up several floors in height. Four powered staircases, one for each of the warehouse's walls, provided access to the collection of mechanical equipment. Armaments and specialty equipment were kept primarily on the easternmost wall, and within a secure room located close by.<ref name="TLJ" />

Around [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], the store and its owner sold a selection of equipment to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Shortly thereafter, a [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] by the name of [[Den Dhur]] came to the Keldabe retailer for parts to upgrade his droid companion, [[I-5YQ]]. Upon learning of the business's recent transactions with the Empire, Dhur—an ally of the anti-Imperial organization known as [[Whiplash]]—offered to reward the proprietor with additional [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] for a manifest of what goods the Empire had purchased.<ref name="TLJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
The nameless warehouse store in Keldabe first introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe via an appearance in the novel [[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']], co-written by [[Author/Legends|authors]] [[Michael Reaves]] and [[Maya Kaathryn Bohnhoff]], and published [[February 26]], [[2013]].
